summary:
Mars Colony: Mission Survival is a strategy game for children aged 7 to 12, built in Unity. The player leads four astronauts who have just landed on Mars and must keep them alive for 30 sols. To do that, they build and manage six structures: a shielded habitat, solar arrays, batteries, an oxygen generator, a greenhouse and an ice drill.

The game answers the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge by teaching through play instead of text. It gives one goal at a time and points to the next step, so children discover for themselves why a crew needs oxygen, water, food, power and radiation shielding. Three emergencies (a dust storm, a solar radiation storm and an equipment failure) pause the game and ask the player to choose between three options, each with a cost. The radiation storms are taken from 27 real 2024 events in NASA's DONKI database.

This matters because the children playing today are the generation that may go to Mars. The game runs in English and Arabic, so Arabic-speaking children can learn real space science in their own language.
details:
Mars Colony: Mission Survival is a 3D educational survival simulation game developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

The project challenges players to establish and manage a sustainable human colony on Mars while facing the environmental and engineering challenges of living on another planet.

Players must manage essential resources, including oxygen, water, food, battery energy, and construction materials. They can construct and operate facilities such as solar arrays, battery storage systems, oxygen generators, greenhouses, shielded habitats, and ice drills.

The game features realistic Mars-inspired challenges, including dust storms that reduce solar energy production, solar radiation events that threaten astronaut safety, equipment failures, and limited resources.

Players must make strategic decisions to maintain life-support systems, protect astronauts from radiation, generate electricity, produce oxygen, grow food, and ensure the colony’s survival.

The simulation incorporates scientific concepts such as In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU), oxygen production inspired by NASA’s MOXIE experiment, radiation shielding, and sustainable energy management.

Developed using Unity 6 and the Universal Render Pipeline (URP), the project transforms complex space exploration concepts into an interactive learning experience that promotes critical thinking, problem-solving, engineering awareness, and resource management.

The ultimate goal is to help players understand the challenges of establishing a sustainable human presence on Mars through engaging and educational gameplay.
